title: When she stops texting after a great date
situation: The date went well. Conversation flowed. Now it's been 1–2 days with no message.
insight: Silence doesn't always mean disinterest. People pull back for many reasons—timing, uncertainty, or simply waiting to see what you do. The risk isn't reaching out. The risk is overcorrecting.

title: What to wear on a first date
situation: You want to make a strong impression but don't want to look like you're trying too hard.
insight: Attraction is often about ease. The goal isn't to impress—it's to feel natural and put together. If you're adjusting your clothes all night, it's the wrong choice.
quick_reference: Keep it simple (1 strong piece max)
Clean shoes matter more than you think

title: You think you came on too strong
situation: After the interaction, you're replaying things and feel like you may have overdone it.
insight: Overthinking after the fact is common. Most people don't remember intensity as much as they remember how they felt. Trying to "fix it" too quickly often makes it worse.
quick_reference: Don't send a correction text immediately
Let the next interaction reset the tone

title: What to text after a first date
situation: The date ended well. Now you're unsure what to say—or when to say it.
insight: The follow-up should match the tone of the date. You're not trying to escalate—you're continuing the same energy.
quick_reference: Reference something specific from the date

title: You're not sure if she's interested
situation: Responses are inconsistent. Sometimes engaged, sometimes distant.
insight: Interest shows up in consistency, not intensity. Mixed signals are often low or uncertain interest—not a puzzle to solve.
quick_reference: Match her effort, don't exceed it
Don't try to "win her over" through volume
If it feels one-sided, it probably is

title: When she cancels plans last minute
situation: Plans were set. She cancels close to the time, often with a vague reason.
insight: Interest doesn't disappear—it shows up in effort. A cancellation without a clear reschedule is a signal, not an inconvenience.
quick_reference: Don't chase a new time immediately
Let her suggest the next plan
One cancel = data point, not a pattern (yet)

title: How often you should text
situation: You're unsure how much communication is too much or too little.
insight: There is no perfect frequency—only matching energy. Over-texting usually comes from trying to secure interest instead of letting it develop.
quick_reference: Don't text just to fill space

title: When conversation feels forced
situation: You're running out of things to say, or it feels like work to keep it going.
insight: Good connection doesn't require constant effort. If you're forcing conversation, you're likely trying to maintain something that isn't naturally there.
quick_reference: Shift topics or end it naturally
Pay attention to how often this happens

title: Talking about past relationships
situation: The topic comes up early, and you're unsure how much to share.
insight: Early conversations aren't about full disclosure—they're about tone. Oversharing creates weight too soon; avoiding entirely can feel guarded.

title: When she takes a long time to respond
situation: Hours—or days—between replies. You're unsure if it means disinterest.
insight: Response time reflects priority more than intention. People respond quickly to what they're excited about.
